workflow.title: Choose next month’s growth commitment
workflow.question: Which growth plan can we afford to carry out?
workflow.description: Compare four complete growth commitments against cash after every dated payment and receipt, a required reserve, delivery hours, collection timing and the complete obligation horizon. definition.title: Complete a commitment
definition.description: Determine whether one complete static plan can satisfy every mandatory obligation across every explicitly admitted scenario. Compare feasible plans only after whole-plan execution feasibility is established.

authoring.guidance:
What must be completed, for whom, and within which accepted limits?
Which objects, quantities, revisions and locations are covered?
Which factual records and admitted states are we relying on?
Which complete choices may the planner make?
Which activities, dependencies, calendars and capacities must the same plan respect?
Which scoped permissions must cover each required operation?
Which joint operating scenarios must this commitment withstand?
Which obligations are mandatory, and how will passing complete plans be compared?
Module authors supply these declarations and domain vocabulary. Case workers supply only values allowed by the frozen module. Facts, scenarios and operating permission must never be inferred from a preferred plan.
Activities may be empty when explicit period-capacity predicates completely describe the bounded workload. Ordered customer receipts and payments use the opt-in ordered-cash-flow/1 contract; expense and cash movement remain distinct.

definition.title: Complete a commitment
definition.responsibility: Find one complete static operating choice that satisfies every mandatory obligation across every explicitly admitted joint scenario, then compare feasible choices.
invariants: Choices are finite, input-only controls. One complete assignment is shared across every admitted scenario and obligation.
Admitted joint scenarios are explicit facts; neither independence, probabilities nor unlisted scenarios are inferred.
An empty admitted basis is inconsistent, never a vacuous feasibility result.
Typed acyclic expressions separate static controls, scenario consequences and post-scenario preference aggregates.
Activities, calendars, bookings and permission validity use half-open intervals; adjacent intervals do not overlap.
Capacity is the sum of simultaneous renewable demands. A scoped grant must cover its entire required operation.
Expense sums nonrefundable charges. Refundable holds affect cash only; simultaneous cash events are netted before peak cash is measured.
Every mandatory condition must pass for the same choice in every admitted scenario. Preference cannot compensate for failure.
Ranking is lexicographic over feasible choices only; genuine ties are retained and identifiers only stabilize display order.
A fully checked witness establishes existence during partial search. No-plan and optimality claims require complete relevant coverage.
Missing data, unresolved lookups, unsafe arithmetic and unsupported declarations are invalid input, never invented facts.
Calculated feasibility is conditional on accepted facts and fixed assumptions, not permission, reservation or evidence of actual completion.

expressionLanguage.literals: Finite scalar or homogeneous scalar-array data; no executable code.

operators.add: At least two compatible numbers -> number
operators.mul: Two numbers with at most one dimensional operand -> number; count is a multiplicity
operators.lookup: Complete primary-key binding in a typed input table -> exactly one selected scalar; missing or ambiguous lookup is invalid
operators.exists: Typed equality bindings plus optional row-scoped predicate -> boolean; no match is false
operators.interval-covered: Typed selected calendar rows and a positive half-open interval -> boolean; adjacent coverage may combine
operators.worst-case: Numeric expression -> maximum across admitted scenarios for preference only; nested or unreduced scenario aggregates are invalid

module.title: Compare growth arrangements
module.question: Which growth commitments can we fund and deliver under the declared demand and collection situations?
module.description: Compare a current-approach baseline and three complete growth arrangements against cash by date, a required reserve, delivery capacity and a commitment cutoff. Forecast customer counts are uncertain situations, not controllable sales or probabilities. A passing arrangement is operationally supportable under these inputs; no most-profitable option is selected.

units.timeOrigin: elapsed whole days from the declared growth-planning origin

assumptions: This is an incremental growth calculation for one standard service package. Opening cash is already unrestricted growth funding after existing obligations; do not deduct those obligations again. The minimum reserve is an additional balance that must remain available.

Each arrangement has a fixed committed campaign expense that remains payable when sales disappoint. Forecast customer counts determine delivery expense, receipts and workload. Costs are not automatically inferred from customer-acquisition ratios.

Every declared situation supplies a complete joint forecast for all alternatives. Passing requires meeting every retained requirement in every declared situation; no probability of success or guarantee of customer demand is inferred.

Cash uses explicit elapsed days and ordered atomic events. On the same day, campaign payment occurs first, delivery payment second, and customer receipt third. A later receipt cannot fund an earlier payment. Customer receipts are not treated as negative expenses or returned deposits.

The payment-before-delivery alternative receives its complete customer price no later than delivery starts. Invoice alternatives collect no earlier than delivery finishes. The model assumes full receipt on each declared collection date; bad debt, refunds, tax and recognition rules require an authored extension.

Capacity is available incremental hours in the explicitly identified delivery period. All customer work fits inside that period. The model does not spread work across periods, infer staffing from elapsed time, or solve a detailed task schedule.

The comparison horizon must contain every payment, receipt and delivery completion. A multi-period contract needs its complete obligations inside this model or a new authored profile; its first month cannot stand for the whole commitment.

The baseline represents no incremental campaign and no incremental customers. Its zero cash events are harmless placeholders. Feasibility-only comparison neither recommends a growth target nor estimates campaign effectiveness or causal impact.

module.title: Assess a payment-terms test
module.description: Compare choosing a fundable and deliverable growth arrangement now with a nonbinding payment-preference test and a complete response to each possible signal.
module.question: Could a timely preference test improve the growth choice enough to cover its cost?
module.boundary: One nonbinding preference test followed by one complete growth arrangement. Customer orders, collected deposits, refunds and adaptive marketing campaigns are outside this model.

objective.beneficiary: The business funding and delivering the growth commitment
objective.horizon: The complete declared campaign and customer delivery horizon

assumptions: The prior and likelihood matrix are explicit fictional teaching inputs. A survey signal is an imperfect observation of a declared situation; it is not a causal estimate of additional customers.

Net contribution for each action and situation comes from the same pinned planning assessment: customer receipts less delivery expense and committed campaign expense. The test fee is charged once, separately.
The test accepts no payment, order or deposit and creates no customer delivery obligation. A paid pilot requires a different complete operating model.
All declared situations remain logically possible after every report, including an inconclusive report. Zero probabilities never waive funding, capacity or timing conditions.
Operating eligibility comes from current native commitment runs for acting now and acting after the test fee and delay. A profitable action cannot compensate for an operating failure.

The baseline is a complete no-expansion alternative. An expected-contribution preference is supplied only for this optional learning comparison; feasibility alone does not select a growth arrangement.

questions.label: Cash available at the start
questions.question: How much cash is available before this growth commitment?
questions.meaning: Available opening cash in minor currency units after obligations outside this case have already been accounted for. Do not subtract those obligations again.

questions.label: Minimum cash reserve
questions.question: What minimum cash balance must remain available?
questions.meaning: A minimum balance maintained after every ordered payment or receipt, including intermediate events on the same date.

questions.label: Collected price per customer
questions.question: How much will each customer pay for the standardized package?
questions.meaning: Full collected price per customer in minor currency units. Collection timing is declared separately for every arrangement and situation.

questions.label: Delivery expense per customer
questions.question: What additional delivery expense does one customer create?
questions.meaning: Incremental complete delivery expense per customer in minor currency units. The campaign expense is committed separately and does not shrink when fewer customers buy.

questions.label: Delivery effort per customer
questions.question: How many delivery hours does each customer require?
questions.meaning: Whole delivery hours per standardized customer package. Only capacity within the declared delivery period supports that work.

questions.label: Current decision day
questions.question: On which day can we make the growth commitment?
questions.meaning: Whole elapsed days from the declared origin. All nonzero operating cash events must still be in the future at commitment time.

questions.label: Growth commitment cutoff
questions.question: By which day must we commit to an expansion arrangement?
questions.meaning: Latest elapsed day for a growth arrangement. The no-expansion alternative remains available after this cutoff.

questions.label: Complete comparison horizon
questions.question: Through which day does this comparison include cash and delivery?
questions.meaning: All nonzero payments, receipts and complete customer delivery must lie within this horizon. Extending a contract requires its full obligations, not only a favorable first month.

questions.label: Contribution target above campaign expense
questions.question: How much contribution must remain after campaign expense?
questions.meaning: A stated monetary hurdle above recovering the committed campaign expense. This target does not predict how many genuinely additional customers will be acquired.

questions.label: Committed campaign expenses
questions.question: What campaign expense is committed for each arrangement?
questions.meaning: Complete campaign expense in minor currency units, paid independently of customer response. Arrangement identities and payment-term meanings are fixed by the authored app.

questions.label: Declared operating situations
questions.question: Which demand and collection situations must the arrangements withstand?
questions.meaning: Explicit joint situations, not probability samples. Every arrangement needs exactly one complete outcome in every declared situation.

questions.label: Customers, collection and delivery
questions.question: What customers, cash dates and delivery work are assumed in each situation?
questions.meaning: Customer count, complete payment and receipt dates, delivery interval and capacity period for every arrangement and situation. These are declared assumptions; the app does not forecast sales.

questions.label: Available delivery capacity
questions.question: How many hours are available in the delivery period?
questions.meaning: Available hours during the specified complete period, after other work has been accounted for once. Work must fit inside that period as well as within its available hours.

questions.label: Compare a preference test
questions.question: Should we also calculate the value of a nonbinding preference test?
questions.meaning: Optional expected-contribution analysis. Missing probabilities or test assumptions do not prevent the operating comparison.

questions.label: Test and probability assumptions
questions.question: Which test cost, delay, probabilities and signal likelihoods are defensible?
questions.meaning: Explicit priors and a complete likelihood matrix for the two authored payment-response situations. The nonbinding test collects no money or orders. Its fee and elapsed days are counted before the complete response.
